input.title: Get your recommendation
input.targetYieldHelp: Leave blank if you are not sure — we will estimate a typical target for this crop.
input.soilSectionDesc: Enter values from your soil health card, or upload the report below.
input.orPasteText: or paste the text from your report
input.pleaseCheckValues: Please check these values before continuing — automatic reading is not always perfect.
input.weatherAutoFilled: Filled in automatically for your location. You may edit these.
input.priceSectionDesc: If you have heard of recent price changes, tell us here.
input.mixerDesc: Move the sliders — the three always add up to 100%.
input.mixerSentenceEco: We will lean towards organic and low-runoff options even if they cost more.
input.mixerSentenceBalanced: We will balance sustainability, cost and yield fairly evenly.
input.mixerSentenceBudget: We will lean towards the cheapest workable option.
input.mixerSentenceYield: We will lean towards options that push yield higher, within safe limits.
input.numberBetween: Please enter a number between {{min}} and {{max}}

recommendation.title: Your recommendation
recommendation.noDeficiencyTitle: Your soil looks sufficient for now
recommendation.noDeficiencyBody: We would suggest no fertilizer at the moment, and re-testing next season.
recommendation.weatherDisagreeNote: The weather outlook and your soil report did not fully agree — we followed your soil report.
recommendation.whyTopPickChanged: Why this plan moved to the top
recommendation.priceAlternativeNote: Prices may rise — you may consider this alternative
recommendation.deferApplicationNote: Heavy rain is expected — you may consider waiting a few days before applying.
recommendation.riskWarningNote: This dose is closer to the safe limit. We recommend a soil lab test before applying.
recommendation.nextRotationTitle: Next crop rotation and soil health
recommendation.nutrientUseEfficiencyMeaning: How much of the applied nutrient the crop is likely to use, rather than lose.
recommendation.emissionsMeaning: Greenhouse-gas impact of this plan, in CO2-equivalent per hectare.
recommendation.surplusMeaning: Nutrient applied beyond what the crop is likely to take up.
recommendation.disclaimer: These are estimates to guide you, not guaranteed results. A soil lab test and local agriculture officer advice are recommended.
recommendation.basedOn: Based on your soil report and local weather near {{district}}
recommendation.sustainabilityMeaningGood: This plan is in good shape for the environment, with efficient nutrient use and low surplus.
recommendation.sustainabilityMeaningModerate: This plan is reasonable, but there is room to make it more sustainable.
recommendation.sustainabilityMeaningNeedsImprovement: This plan could be made considerably greener — see the suggestions below.
recommendation.improveSwitchScore: Switching to the {{plan}} would raise the score from {{from}} to {{to}}.
recommendation.improveCutEmissions: The {{plan}} would cut emissions by about {{pct}}%.

explain.title: Why did we decide this?
explain.subtitle: A step-by-step look at how we built your recommendation
explain.step1Desc: We compared your N, P and K values against typical cut-offs for this crop.
explain.step2Desc: We also look at weather patterns before your soil report arrives, then check if they agree.
explain.step3Desc: We estimated the nutrient balance this crop typically needs for your target yield.
explain.step4Desc: Recent rain and temperature trends nudged the dose slightly, within a safety limit of 20%.
explain.step5Desc: We checked the plan would not go far beyond safe application limits.
explain.step6Desc: We compared plans on cost and sustainability, including recent price trends.
explain.step7Desc: We estimated a likely yield range and what pushed it up or down.
explain.step8Desc: A blend of nutrient efficiency, emissions and surplus.
explain.step9Desc: An honest look at how sure we are, and what this estimate is based on.
explain.syntheticDataNote: This model is partly trained on synthetic (simulated) data and should be treated as a helpful estimate, not a lab result.
explain.technicalShap: Technical detail: these factors come from a SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) feature-attribution analysis.
